headline: Revenue rises, but hedging losses sink earnings
summary_short: Net income fell 53.8% year-over-year to $51.9M ($0.13 diluted EPS), even as revenue grew 22.5% to $512.5M; corporate hedging/interest-expense losses and an unfavorable swing in residential-loan fair value outweighed gains in the Property and Investing & Servicing segments.
summary_long: Revenue grew on Property segment growth (Fundamental's net lease acquisitions) and higher Investing & Servicing default-interest fees, partly offset by lower Infrastructure Lending interest income. Despite the top line growing, GAAP net income fell to $51.9M as Corporate losses widened to $164.6M on higher unsecured-note interest expense and swap losses, and Commercial & Residential Lending swung to a $12.9M other-loss on unfavorable residential-loan fair value and FX moves. Distributable Earnings — the REIT's dividend-coverage metric — fell to $0.39/share from $0.42/share, below the $0.48/share dividend declared. The board authorized a $400M buyback in February 2026 and repurchased $19.9M of stock in March. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Corporate segment losses widened on higher unsecured-note interest expense and interest-rate-swap losses, and Commercial & Residential Lending swung to an other-loss on unfavorable residential-loan fair value and FX moves, outweighing growth in the Property and Investing & Servicing segments.

Corporate segment loss widened to $164.6 million on higher unsecured-note/term-loan interest expense and swap losses; Commercial & Residential Lending other income swung to a $12.9 million loss on unfavorable residential-loan fair value and FX moves.

Property segment revenue rose on Fundamental's net lease acquisitions and Investing & Servicing revenue grew on higher default-interest servicing fees, partly offset by lower Infrastructure Lending interest income from lower average balances and index rates.
EPS fell faster than net income because diluted weighted-average shares outstanding rose 9.4% year-over-year (366.9M vs 335.5M), diluting the smaller net income across more shares.

Tracks the same corporate interest-expense increase and segment mix shift that reduced GAAP net income, since Distributable Earnings excludes only unrealized/non-cash items, not the underlying operating and financing cost changes.

The filing's broader 'cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash' fell only $8.7 million q/q to $666.1 million; the sharper drop in unrestricted cash alone implies a shift into restricted cash, not an overall liquidity decline.
